close_reason: Extracted classify_message() pure function. Binary frames now surface UnexpectedResponse immediately per RFC 8887 §4.1. Ping/Pong/other still silently skipped but capped at MAX_CONSECUTIVE_NON_TEXT_FRAMES=64 to prevent server-side starvation. 5 new unit tests cover the classification policy. Workspace tests green.
description: src/ws/mod.rs:94 — `Ok(_) => continue, // Ping / Pong / Binary: silently skip`. RFC 8887 §4.1 says JMAP only uses text frames; ignoring Ping/Pong is correct (tungstenite handles them at the protocol layer). But a misbehaving or hostile server that sends a continuous stream of Binary frames would cause this loop to spin forever inside a single `next_frame` call. There is no bound on iterations, and no timeout. Fix options: (a) cap consecutive Binary skips and yield an UnexpectedResponse error, (b) document the loop bound is governed by tungstenite's max_message_size (which is 1 MiB and would close the connection on oversized frames), (c) yield Unknown for Binary so the caller sees them. Note: locked crate.
title: WsSession::next_frame silently skips Binary frames; can starve a caller indefinitely
